seo.title: Merchant Center Product Data: Required Attributes
seo.meta_description: The Merchant Center product data Google requires: title, description, image, price, availability, brand, GTIN and condition, for Orange County retailers.

h1: Merchant Center Product Data: The Attributes That Get Products Shown
answer: Merchant Center product data is the information Google uses to show your products, including required attributes such as title, description, image link, price and availability, plus brand, GTIN and condition where they apply. Titles can be up to 150 characters, and Google will require product images of at least 500 by 500 pixels from January 31, 2027. Anaheim and Orange County retailers should get these right first.
key_takeaways: Title, description, image, price and availability are required.
Images will need to be at least 500 x 500 from Jan 31, 2027.
Brand is required for most new products.
GTINs are strongly recommended where available.

sections.heading: Why product data matters
sections.body_html: Google uses your product data to decide which searches your products match. Clear, accurate data helps products appear for the right shoppers; poor data leads to issues and disapprovals.

sections.heading: Why it matters for Orange County retailers
sections.body_html: Shoppers in Anaheim and across Orange County often search Google before visiting a store or buying online, and Google shows products in Search, the Shopping tab, Maps, Images, Lens, YouTube and Gemini. Merchant Center is how your products get there. For independent shops competing with big chains, accurate product data is one of the few places where a small retailer can look just as complete as a large one.

sections.heading: Title
sections.body_html: Google's specification says the title is required, plain text, up to 150 characters. Its example is Mens Pique Polo Shirt. Include what the product is and key details shoppers search for, such as brand, size or color.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body_html: The description is required. Google's example describes material, fit, features and care. Describe the product accurately, as you would to a customer in the store.

sections.heading: Image link
sections.body_html: The main image URL is required, must start with http or https and must be crawlable by Google. Google has announced that product images must be at least 500 x 500 pixels, with enforcement starting January 31, 2027.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.body_html: Availability is required, with values such as in stock, out of stock, preorder and backorder. Google says it must match your landing page, checkout and structured data, and the price must stay visible even when an item is out of stock.

sections.heading: Brand
sections.body_html: Brand is required for all new products except movies, books and musical recordings, up to 70 characters. Google says to use your own brand only if you manufacture the product or it's a generic brand category.

sections.heading: GTIN
sections.body_html: Google strongly recommends a GTIN, such as a 12-digit UPC in North America, where one exists. It helps Google identify exactly what you sell.

sections.heading: Condition
sections.body_html: Condition is required for used or refurbished products and optional for new ones. Google defines refurbished as professionally restored to working order with a warranty.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Titles that are just a model number.
  • Images blocked by robots.txt.
  • Availability that doesn't match the website.
  • Using your store name as the brand for products you don't make.
  • Missing GTINs for branded products.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask how long titles should be. Use the space to describe the product clearly, up to Google's 150-character limit, starting with the most important details. Another common question is whether to use manufacturer descriptions. They're a starting point, but adding your own helpful details makes listings more useful and less identical to other sellers. Owners also ask about the new image size rule. Check that your main product images are at least 500 by 500 pixels well before Google's January 31, 2027 enforcement date, and replace any that aren't.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Titles descriptive and under 150 characters.
  • Descriptions accurate.
  • Images at least 500 x 500.
  • Availability matches the site.
  • Brand correct.
  • GTINs added where available.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a skate shop in Costa Mesa whose product titles are just codes like SK-2241. The owner rewrites them as brand, product type, size and color, adds UPCs from the packaging and replaces small images with 1200-pixel photos. Disapprovals for missing data drop, and products start matching searches for specific decks and sizes.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: This task is one piece of a wider local plan. Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity, so the profile, your website and your reputation all have to agree. A practical order for most Orange County businesses is: get the Business Profile verified and accurate, make the name, address and phone identical everywhere, publish one clear page per service, then build a steady habit of genuine reviews and replies. Each step makes the next one work better, and the same signals help AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI features describe your business correctly when someone in Anaheim asks for a recommendation.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Export your product data.
  2. Rewrite your top 20 titles.
  3. Check image sizes.
  4. Add missing GTINs.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Most of this can be done in-house with an hour or two and careful reading of Google's own help pages. It is worth bringing in help when the stakes are high or the problem keeps coming back: a profile that has been suspended more than once, many locations to manage, a site that keeps failing the same checks, or no time to keep up the routine. A good local SEO partner should explain what they will change and why, point to Google's guidelines rather than promise rankings, and leave you with access to every account. Chimera works this way with businesses across Anaheim and Orange County.

sections.heading: Writing better descriptions
sections.body_html: A good description answers the questions a shopper would ask a staff member. What is it made of? What size or fit is it? What's included in the box? How is it cared for or used? Write in plain sentences, put the most important details first and avoid all-caps, promotional language or links. If many sellers use the same manufacturer text, adding a line about how customers in your store use the product makes yours more helpful.

sections.heading: Keeping data in sync
sections.body_html: The most common data problems come from changes that reach your website but not your product data, such as a sale price, a sold-out item or a new photo. Use your platform's automatic sync where possible, and if you upload files, schedule them to run at least daily. After any big change, like a seasonal sale or new collection, check a handful of products in Merchant Center to confirm they match your site.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Get the required attributes right, write descriptive titles, use large crawlable images and match availability to your site. Chimera, based in Anaheim, audits product data for Orange County retailers.
